newsitem.title: UK: Middle East tanker rates fall in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Middle East tanker rates fall in thin trade.

text.p: Tanker rates in the key Middle East Gulf slipped on Monday amid thin activity in all lifting sectors, brokers said.
An industry conference attended by many oil market participants in Singapore this week was seen primarily responsible for the lackustre chartering activity, brokers said.
In the Middle East Gulf, rates fell on all routes out of the region. Brokers noted a bearish downside on VLCCs bound for Japan, seen to be off four Worldscale points at W60 from last done levels.
Western voyages could only command W50 whilst rates for VLCCs travelling East slumped to W58, off five points.

Although no ULCC chartering was seen, two VLCCs found employment westwards. By mid-afternoon, Petrobras' chartering of a 280,000 tonne cargo on the Borgogne, travelling to Brazil and a VLCC fixed by Petron travelling to Philadelphia were the only vessels seen.
"There are a lot of cargoes still to be lifted in September, whilst charterers are holding back waiting for rates to drop off," a broker said.
This broker said Middle East Gulf rates may drop fractionally further but could bounce back if rates drop as much as five points.

Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med remained around W92.5-95 though as high as W110 was seen. NOC's chartering of the Almare Ottava travelling Zuetina-Sarroch at W110 was not seen as indicative of the market.
In the inter-UKC sector rates were consolidating around the W94 level amidst a dearth of fixtures.
By mid-afternoon, brokers confirmed that not a single vessel had been fixed in this sector.
